preamble: Correspondence of the voiced retroflex fricative [ʐ] with the voiced alveolar fricative [z] in Polish dialects with mazurzenie (Masovia, Masuria, most of Lesser Poland, parts of Silesia), where the standard retroflex series /ʂ, ʐ, t͡ʂ, d͡ʐ/ is merged with the dentals, so ż [ʐ] is [z]. Its origin is debated: Koneczna derives it directly from the 16th-century depalatalization of the older palato-alveolars /ʃ, ʒ, t͡ʃ, d͡ʒ/, which gave retroflexes elsewhere but dentals here, while Kuryłowicz argues that archaic dialects adopted the new retroflexes and replaced them with dentals. It is treated here as a synchronic dialect correspondence of standard Polish retroflex cz, sz, ż, dż [t͡ʂ ʂ ʐ d͡ʐ] to mazurating c, s, z, dz. The ż from the old trill rz is excluded, since rz became [ʐ] later and stays [ʐ] (rzucać [ʐut͡sat͡ɕ] in both dialect types). Outside Polish the feature was borrowed by a few Belarusian villages in Podlachia.

examples.note: Mazurating dialects merge the postalveolar/retroflex sibilants with the dentals.
Both ż [ʐ] and dż are fronted in the same word.

sources: Gogolewski, S. (2001). Dialectology in Poland, 1873–1997. In Koerner, E. F. K. & Szwedek, A. (eds.), Towards a History of Linguistics in Poland. John Benjamins. https://doi.org/10.1075/sihols.102.07gog
